label: L-02
title: The post-broadcast `:preview` 'verification' re-executes any outstanding step under prank instead of asserting it is already done, so a partial or diverged mainnet cutover verifies green
fingerprintProvenance: Copied verbatim from reports/31/script-audits/stable-staker-v2-cutover/classified-findings.json (not recomputed). finding-manager cross-check: sha256(fingerprintBasis) reproduces it byte-for-byte.
specConformance: cross-listed (story-082 'Preview doubles as post-broadcast verification' + package.json doc key)
description: The package.json doc key and the story both claim that after a broadcast, `:preview` "re-runs every assertion and smoke test against the live deployment", with every phase detecting "from on-chain state that it is done and skips". In fact every phase is `if (!done) do();`. Preview impersonates OWNER, so any step that did NOT land on mainnet is silently performed inside the simulation, and Phase 8 then asserts the simulated state. Nothing in preview mode, not even with a progress file loaded, requires that zero mutations were needed. The per-user loss bound is also evaluated only over `plan.migratable` from the same leg, which is empty after a broadcast, so the on-chain credits are never re-checked. This is the run-22 `ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast` family: all planning and assertions run in forge's local pass, and the batches are frozen there, before the Ledger session sends ~47 transactions with `--slow --skip-simulation`. A V1 `stake` that lands after the local pass but before the Phase-1 `pause()` transaction (cf. ledger c04da307336c on promotion-ready) is absent from every batch. Phase 7 then revokes V1's phUSD mint anyway, which bricks that user's `userMigrate` while their frozen pending is non-zero. The chained preview then migrates them in simulation and reports success.
impact: The operator's only automated outcome check can report a finished cutover while mainnet has V1 phUSD mint still live, V2 still paused, or a staker stranded on V1 behind a revoked mint. Remedies exist (owner re-grant plus re-run), but nothing surfaces the need for them. No direct loss is proven. Mainnet per-user loss stays bounded by the strategies' own minOut floors.
attackPath: 1. Broadcast: forge's local pass plans and freezes about 47 transactions, then the Ledger session sends them with --slow --skip-simulation.
2. Some step does not land, e.g. setMinter(V1,false) or v2.unpause(), or a V1 stake lands between the local pass and the Phase-1 pause tx and is absent from every frozen batch.
3. The operator runs :preview to verify; every phase is if(!done) do() under vm.startPrank(OWNER), so the missing step is performed in simulation.
4. Phase 8 asserts the simulated state and prints output byte-identical to a clean run (fork-verified: MASK_REVOKE and MASK_PAUSED_V2 both PASS).

classification.assetImpact: No direct loss. A partial or diverged broadcast (V1 phUSD mint still live, V2 still paused, or a staker stranded on V1 behind a revoked mint) can be reported as a clean verification, so recoverable misconfigurations go unnoticed.

classification.likelihood: low-medium - requires a broadcast to partially fail or a stake to race the pre-pause window; both are realistic for a 47-tx Ledger session but not attacker-forced.
classification.assumptions: Operator relies on :preview as the post-broadcast outcome check, as the doc key instructs.
classification.externalRequirements: A dropped or failed broadcast transaction, or a staker racing the local-pass-to-pause window.
remediesEnumerated: Every masked state is owner-recoverable in 1-2 transactions (re-revoke the mint, unpause V2, re-grant V1 mint so the stranded user can userMigrate, then revoke again), but nothing surfaces the need.

severityRationale: Same class as fix-pending M-01 2c53e944caee (VerificationRunsAgainstSimulatedNotBroadcastState) on promotion-ready:broadcast. That entry stood at Medium because no verification existed at all; here a verification exists but self-heals, it degrades a compensating control, every masked state is owner-recoverable, and no asset loss is shown. That places it at Low, consistent with the run-22 L-level members of the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family. It is a class recurrence: the story-075 assert-only verifier pattern was not carried forward. Tagged faithfulness because the story and doc key claim a live-state re-verification that does not happen.
recommendation: Add a separate assert-only verifier (mirroring story-075's standalone VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol) or an explicit VERIFY_ONLY env-flag mode that never calls vm.startPrank/vm.startBroadcast and never mutates. Gate it on ON-CHAIN state, not on the progress file: do NOT key verify-only mode off progress-file deploymentStatus == completed, because progress files can be stamped completed during forge's local pass (ledger 1e8cc0dc58ba). In that mode every phase must require(alreadyDone, 'verify: step X not on chain') and never perform it. Live asserts must include: V1 phUSD mint revoked, V2 and Antimatter unpaused, V1 stakerCount/totalStaked per pool <= the straggler allow-list, V2 pauser == Pauser, and the Antimatter minter set. Re-check the per-user loss bound from on-chain receipts (V1 MigratedOut / V2 DepositedFor events, or persisted pre-migration principals) against V2 userInfo rather than the empty same-leg plan. Separately, assert that the set of V1 stakers at the Phase-1 pause block equals the frozen planning set, and fail loudly if a staker raced the window.
evidence: Code: Phase 7 `if (_canMintPhUSD(STABLE_STAKER_V1)) { IPhUSDOwner(PHUSD).setMinter(STABLE_STAKER_V1, false); ... }` and `if (v2.paused()) v2.unpause();`, both executed under `vm.startPrank(OWNER)` in preview. Per-user check loop `for (uint256 i = 0; i < plan.migratable.length; i++)` (Core:440). Fork @25975869, harness inheriting the unmodified script: (C) after a full cutover, `phUSD.setMinter(V1,true)` (revoke 'did not land') then `run()` in PREVIEW_MODE -> `[PASS] ... MASK_REVOKE|preview run() PASSED although V1 phUSD mint was live on-chain` (log shows 'REVOKED' again, fork-logs/h-test_C_previewMasksMissingRevoke.log). (C2) Pauser pauses V2 ('unpause did not land') then `run()` -> `MASK_PAUSED_V2|preview run() PASSED although V2 was paused on-chain`. The console output is byte-identical to a clean verification ('V1 pauser -> Pauser and V1 unpaused (inert); V2 + Antimatter registered with Pauser; V2 unpaused'), fork-logs/h-test_C2_previewMasksPausedV2.log.
